tasks.short: Diagram supply chain flows for customer discussions.

steps.what: Agree the customer question, scope and level of detail.
Retrieve locations, stock movements and service constraints.
Reconcile location names and assemble the network table.
Draw locations, routes, handoffs and explanatory labels.
Check operational accuracy and approve the customer view.
Discuss the diagram and capture customer corrections or alternatives.

tasks.design: A reusable generator accepts exports from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, validates location mappings and renders a diagram in the {DOCS}. Start with file uploads; add scheduled retrieval through the {DATA_PLATFORM} where access permits. The manager approves the customer view and leads the discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Location identifiers differed, and each diagram was manually redrawn for its audience.
tasks.enabler_now: Established graph layout libraries and reusable data mappings make generation practical. AI coding can shorten connector and template development; no model is needed during normal use.
tasks.still_hard: Records omit informal handoffs, temporary routes and commercially sensitive details. Choosing the right abstraction remains contextual.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the customer is worried about and explain the operational tradeoffs honestly.

ambition.what: Customer route-change comparison showing the current network beside one proposed alternative.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time drawing and more time testing customer alternatives. No new commercial approval rights are assumed.

reach.task: Validate route and throughput assumptions for customer scenarios.
reach.learn: Network data modelling, flow reconciliation and clear visual explanation.

evidence.claim: Structured network tables can drive repeatable diagrams with deterministic layout and validation.
Customer framing and approval of commercially sensitive diagrams remain human work.

assumptions: The first release covers one network and a small set of diagram templates.
Stable location identifiers or an approved mapping can be supplied.
The diagram represents operations; it does not claim to optimise the network.
GDPR applies if extracts contain personal data; customer diagrams exclude unnecessary personal fields.
unknowns: Which exports and read permissions are available?
How much reconciliation and redrawing occurs today?
Who approves disclosure of routes, capacities and supplier locations?
Do national rules require consultation for the proposed data use?
research_questions: Can template layouts remain legible across typical network sizes?
Which missing-data checks prevent misleading customer diagrams?
new_work: Resolve unmapped locations and missing route endpoints.
Maintain mappings and diagram templates.
Review generated diagrams before customer use.
Check connector changes and data freshness.

tasks.short: Evaluate and select technology for inventory tracking and distribution reporting.

steps.what: Agree tracking problems, user needs and acceptance criteria.
Measure current tracking accuracy, reporting delays and operating costs.
Compare existing capabilities and supplier proposals against requirements.

loop.input: Approved requirements, current system documentation and submitted supplier proposals.
loop.output: Requirement-level capability entries with source passages, limitations and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each claimed capability; validate requirement IDs and flag contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; cap document length and route unsupported entries to review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals describe capabilities in varied prose. Rules can validate fields but cannot reliably extract all qualifications.

steps.what: Calculate costs, benefits and sensitivity under agreed assumptions.
Test shortlisted options against representative warehouse and reporting scenarios.
Recommend an option and obtain investment approval.

tasks.design: Configure baseline measures in the {BI} and keep requirements, evidence and option scores in the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded extraction loop drafts source-linked proposal comparisons; deterministic calculations compare configuration, extension and replacement options. People test the shortlist and approve the investment before procurement proceeds.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evaluation evidence was scattered, proposals used inconsistent language, and cost models were rebuilt for each selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting configuration and reusable scorecards cover much of the work. Bounded document extraction can reduce proposal reading without choosing the supplier.
tasks.still_hard: Migration effort, shop-floor usability and supplier delivery quality are difficult to establish from proposals. Weighted scores cannot settle strategic tradeoffs.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an impressive demonstration from a solution that operators can use reliably.

ambition.what: Quarterly configuration-versus-replacement review of the largest tracking bottleneck.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time observing pilots and challenging assumptions. They gain a repeatable basis for prioritising pilots within their existing budget authority.

reach.task: Assess integration fit and test inventory event handling.
reach.learn: Interface contracts, migration risks and scenario-based acceptance testing.

reach.task: Turn the selected option into a staged implementation plan.
reach.learn: Dependencies, benefit measures and operational rollout sequencing.

evidence.claim: Slim4 provides item-level inventory planning, making existing specialist capability a credible evaluation option.
Lasaulec reported stock reductions above 20% and availability above 98%; the vendor case does not establish transferable benefits.
Requirement scorecards and deterministic cost scenarios can support technology selection; the proposed evaluation assistant is not documented by the cited case.

assumptions: Build estimates cover the evaluation toolkit, not implementation of the selected operational technology.
The comparison includes configuration of existing systems before replacement.
A trial environment and representative, minimised test data are available.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability must be assessed if an option evaluates or monitors workers.
The access range includes initial employee consultation where applicable; national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: What functionality is already licensed but unused?
Which acceptance measures and investment thresholds apply?
Can suppliers provide a representative trial and full cost breakdown?
Will the selected technology change worker monitoring or task allocation?
research_questions: How reliably does extraction preserve exclusions and implementation conditions in proposals?
Which pilot scenarios best reveal scan failures, latency and reconciliation problems?
new_work: Verify extracted capability claims against proposal passages.
Maintain requirements, scoring weights and cost assumptions.
Refresh baseline measures and resolve data gaps.
Maintain reusable pilot scenarios.
Track whether approved benefits appear after implementation.

tasks.short: Identify practical opportunities to reuse materials, recycle waste or create useful by-products.

steps.what: Gather material consumption, scrap, disposal costs and recovery records.
Observe waste streams and ask operators about causes and handling constraints.
Compare material quantities, recovery value and possible internal uses.
Discuss acceptance specifications, transport needs and prices with potential recovery partners.
Assess material suitability, contamination risks and applicable handling requirements.
Select a feasible opportunity and approve a controlled trial.

tasks.design: A small register in the {WORKFLOW} combines material exports from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, disposal costs from the {ERP} and verified recovery specifications. Deterministic calculations rank known reuse options by quantity, net recovery value and stated constraints, with a comparison view in the {BI}. Site observation, technical feasibility and trial approval remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Waste quantities, disposal charges and material specifications were disconnected. Local reuse knowledge rarely became a reusable comparison.
tasks.enabler_now: A lightweight register and repeatable calculations can now be assembled cheaply. This improves preparation without requiring automated material science or legal classification.
tasks.still_hard: Contamination, inconsistent grades, reliable recovery demand and transport economics can defeat a promising calculation. Waste or by-product status needs competent assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice practical opportunities on site and judge whether a recovery route will work safely and consistently.

ambition.what: Provide low-volume sites with a quarterly material recovery opportunity review.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling disposal figures and more time investigating credible recovery routes. They can prioritise trial proposals; technical and spending approvals remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Define acceptance tests for a proposed reused material.
reach.learn: Material traceability, sampling and contamination controls.

reach.task: Calculate collection frequency and net recovery value.
reach.learn: Load consolidation, handling costs and sensitivity to fluctuating volumes.

evidence.claim: A material register and deterministic mass-and-cost calculations can reduce preparation work for recovery assessments.
Operational observations and technical validation remain necessary before approving a reuse or recycling trial.

assumptions: The initial scope covers one material family and known recovery routes.
Rankings indicate investigation priority, not approval for material substitution or waste shipment.
Build estimates exclude laboratory testing, permits and physical process changes.
GDPR applies to any personal data in supporting records; operator-level performance scoring is outside scope.
Employee consultation, where required by national rules, is included in access planning.
unknowns: Are waste quantities measured or estimated?
Which material specifications and contamination tests are available?
Who determines applicable waste or by-product status?
What minimum volumes and acceptance conditions do recovery partners require?
Do proposed trials change working practices enough to require consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which measures distinguish avoided virgin material from a change in disposal destination?
How sensitive is recovery value to contamination, collection frequency and rejected loads?
new_work: Maintain material mappings and recovery specifications.
Check mass balances and missing disposal records.
Refresh partner prices and minimum collection quantities.
Review shortlist exclusions with site and quality teams.
Record trial outcomes before reusing an opportunity elsewhere.

tasks.short: Update supply chain practices when environmental requirements change.

steps.what: Review regulatory notices, standards updates and customer environmental requirements.

loop.input: Dated documents from an approved source list, plus the previous requirements register.
loop.output: Candidate changes with source passages, jurisdiction, dates and unresolved scope questions.
loop.check: Validate source and version; require quoted support; distinguish legal duties from standards and customer terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting material goes to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Obligations and exceptions occur in varied prose. Feed filters can detect documents but cannot reliably extract their meaning.

steps.what: Determine which changes apply to sites, materials and supply chain activities.
Map applicable changes to procedures, controls and responsible teams.
Draft procedure revisions and supporting implementation instructions.

loop.input: Approved applicability assessment, affected procedures and the change impact register.
loop.output: Procedure redlines and implementation instructions linked to approved requirement IDs.
loop.check: Require traceable support for each substantive change; flag missing operational facts and preserve unaffected controls.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unresolved conflicts return to the procedure owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each procedure expresses local practice differently. Templates provide structure but cannot write all contextual revisions.

steps.what: Agree feasible operational changes and approve revised procedures.
Publish approved versions and assign implementation actions to responsible teams.
Check implementation evidence and resolve gaps with site teams.

tasks.design: Configure an approved-source register and requirement-to-procedure links in the {WORKFLOW}, with versioned evidence in the {DOCS}. Bounded loops extract candidate changes and draft redlines after a specialist confirms applicability. Approval triggers publication and actions in the {PROJECT}; the manager checks operational implementation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source monitoring, applicability decisions and procedure updates lived in separate documents and inboxes. Automated drafting lacked dependable links to approved requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control, linked registers and approval workflows are established technology. Bounded extraction and drafting now make document preparation more practical, while specialists retain interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Jurisdiction, exemptions, transition dates and customer terms can interact. A published procedure does not prove that sites have changed their practices.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret uncertain requirements with specialists and negotiate changes that sites can carry out.

ambition.what: A site-specific environmental change brief linking each confirmed requirement to affected procedures and actions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time comparing documents and chasing publication. They can prioritise implementation gaps using linked evidence; legal interpretation and procedure approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate approved environmental requirements into verifiable operating controls.
reach.learn: Requirement traceability, controlled documents and evidence-based control testing.
Dependency mapping, implementation evidence and escalation of overdue actions.

evidence.claim: The digest reports changes to sustainability reporting and due-diligence scope, reinforcing the need for dated applicability assessments.
Linked requirement registers, version control and approval-triggered publication can be configured without autonomous agents.
Source-linked extraction and redline drafting can assist specialists but do not establish legal compliance.

assumptions: The initial release covers one environmental topic and a defined set of sites.
A qualified specialist maintains the authoritative source list and confirms applicability.
Publication requires a recorded approval for the exact document version; later edits invalidate that approval.
GDPR applies to personal data in evidence and action records; EU AI Act applicability is assessed for the actual use.
Consultation about changed working practices follows national rules; the access range allows initial consultation work.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, permits, standards and customer requirements apply?
Who can approve legal applicability and operational procedure changes?
Are procedures versioned and linked to responsible site roles?
Which national employee consultation requirements apply?
What evidence proves implementation at each site?
research_questions: Can candidate-change extraction reliably preserve exemptions and transition dates?
How should withdrawn, amended and conflicting sources be represented?
Which implementation checks distinguish document completion from effective operational change?
new_work: Maintain the approved source list and document versions.
Review extracted changes and unresolved scope questions.
Verify redlines against approved applicability decisions.
Maintain requirement-to-procedure links.
Handle failed publication flows and overdue actions.
Sample implementation evidence and correct ineffective controls.

role.altitude: The supply chain manager spends less time assembling evidence, drawing diagrams and rewriting procedures. More of the week goes to customer scenarios, operational trials and implementation decisions within existing delegated authority.
reach: Logistics analysis: validate network assumptions and quantify recovery economics.
Systems analysis: test operational technology against representative inventory events.
Quality management: define material acceptance tests and verify changed controls.
Project management: sequence trials and coordinate changes across sites.
skills_to_grow: Model operational flows with stable identifiers and explicit assumptions.
Compare options using costs, uncertainty and measurable acceptance criteria.
Review source-linked model outputs and recognise unsupported claims.
Design controlled trials and distinguish activity completion from operational results.
Translate confirmed requirements into practical, verifiable procedures.
role.ambitious_version: Run a recurring supply chain improvement review that brings customer network alternatives, technology pilots and material recovery proposals to decision with comparable evidence.
